findings.evidence: Simple/Basic.lean:72-78; `abbrev IsIrreducible := IsSimpleOrder (Subrepresentation ρ)` at mathlib Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Irreducible.lean:29-31. Mathlib itself registers only the one direction (`instance : IsSimpleModule k[G] ρ.asModule` from `[IsIrreducible ρ]`, Irreducible.lean:51).
findings.fix: Keep only `Rep.simple_of_isIrreducible` as an `instance` and demote `Rep.isIrreducible_of_simple` to a plain theorem (or delete it — `Rep.simple_iff_isIrreducible .mp` already gives it).
findings.issue: `Rep.simple_of_isIrreducible : [IsIrreducible A.ρ] → Simple A` (line 72) and `Rep.isIrreducible_of_simple : [Simple A] → IsIrreducible A.ρ` (line 76) are mutually inverse global instances, so instance search on `Simple A` for `A : Rep k G` descends to `IsSimpleOrder (Subrepresentation A.ρ)` (`IsIrreducible` is an `abbrev` for it, mathlib `RepresentationTheory/Irreducible.lean:29-31`) and back to `Simple A`. Every *failing* `Simple A` or `IsSimpleOrder (Subrepresentation _)` goal now walks that cycle plus the whole `IsSimpleModule`/`IsSimpleOrder` graph before failing.

findings.evidence: Simple/Basic.lean:175-181. Reverse instance used at FDRepClasses.lean:134-136 (to get `IsSimpleModule k[G] X.ρ.asModule` for `simpleModuleClass`). Bypassed by hand at Completeness.lean:208-209 and Completeness.lean:231, both of which write `(FDRep.simple_iff_isIrreducible X).mp` even though `[Simple X]` is already an instance there.
findings.fix: Demote `FDRep.isIrreducible_of_simple` to a plain theorem; supply the one real need in `SimpleFDRepClasses.toSimpleSubmoduleClasses` with `have := (FDRep.simple_iff_isIrreducible X).mp hX` next to the existing `let _ := hX`.
findings.issue: Same defect for `FDRep`: `FDRep.simple_of_isIrreducible` (line 175) and `FDRep.isIrreducible_of_simple` (line 179) form the same cycle. The forward instance is load-bearing (`SimpleFDRepClasses.mk (spechtModule μ)` needs `Simple (spechtModule μ)` from the existing `isIrreducible_spechtModule` instance, SubmoduleTheorem.lean:268); the reverse one has exactly one use, and the PR's own downstream proofs bypass it with an explicit `have` anyway.

summary: The characteristic API and its simp annotations are complete and consistent with the existing `SimpleSubmoduleClasses` sibling, but the dictionary is registered as instances in *both* directions in both `Rep` and `FDRep`, putting a literal cycle into the instance graph. Drop the `isIrreducible_of_simple` direction as instances and keep the iff.
